newsitem.title: INDIA: India call rates rise on repo news, gilt yields up.
newsitem.headline: India call rates rise on repo news, gilt yields up.

text.p: Indian call money rates rallied to close at 10.25-10.75 percent on Thursday, up from the day's opening levels of 6.25-7.00 percent, dealers said.
"Call money jumped to 10.50 percent from 7.0 percent because of the 14 day repo auction annonced by the Reserve Bank of India," Parthasarathi Mukherjee, Chief Dealer at UTI bank, said.
"The market is not sure for the cut-off," he said.
"The repo rate should be between 4.50-5.00 percent, as the cut-off yield on 91 day treasury bills was 6.94 percent," another dealer said.
Volume on National Stock Exchange rose to 1.92 billion rupees against the previous day's 1.39 billion, dealers said.
Yield on 13.50 percent 1997 stock rose to 10.42 percent on Thursday, up from 10.19 percent, dealers said.
Yield on 12 percent 1997 stock was 12.38 percent, compared to previous day's 12.33 percent, dealers said.
Commercial paper for three months maturity were quoted at 11.50-12.25 percent, while certificates of deposit were quoted at 12 percent for one year maturity, dealers at Mata Securities India said.

They said the corporate bonds with 18 months maturity were quoted at 15.0-15.5 percent, 36 months maturity were quoted at 17.0-17.5 percent, while the 60 months maturity were quoted at 18.0-19.0 percent.
